planning_artifacts.TRIAL/.shiploop-runs/seed/worktree/docs/:
# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. Current representative adapter observations are supplied in docs/evidence/adapter.json; reuse them where sufficient.

# Architecture

## Stack
Python standard library and SQLite; installed adapter 2.3 remains the row-application interface.

## Structure
src/adapter.py remains unchanged. Proposed src/__main__.py owns CLI; src/importer.py owns validation, private adapter application, publication and cleanup. Proposed tests/test_import.py owns unit/component/CLI checks. data/ remains read-only. No search feature is requested.
### Namespace and data placement (AD-4..AD-7)
Only execution environment: local Python package src loaded from repository root; tests import src modules. Existing exports: src.adapter.apply and VERSION; src/__init__.py is present. New src.importer.import_json(db_path, file_path) is the CLI's callable seam; validation/staging/publishing helpers are module-private. src.__main__.main(argv=None) handles argparse and calls importer. Use .adapter relative import and standard-library modules; do not create json.py/sqlite3.py or generic utility namespaces. No collisions found in supplied source. No remote environment or persistent configuration to provision.

Authoritative data stays at the selected SQLite file, inventory(sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER), no relationships or new schema/version/migration. Schema creation for a missing DB happens in candidate only through the installed adapter. Existing inventory is cloned by sqlite3.Connection.backup from a read-only source; a fresh candidate starts empty. Importer-owned connections must explicitly close (sqlite3's context manager alone does not close them). Adapter.apply exposes no connection handle; its return proves its synchronous writes/commits have finished, not that its internal idle connection was explicitly closed. For this supported local POSIX/DELETE configuration the candidate must be quiescent (no subsequent adapter writes), with importer-owned handles closed; do not invent an adapter close API or claim the context manager closes it. Candidate must be in a uniquely named owned directory beside destination on the same filesystem; completed candidate uses DELETE journal mode with no outstanding transaction/sidecars before publication. Reject unsupported source modes/path types safely before mutation; no journal-mode conversion on visible DB. Preserve source permissions for replacement; fresh targets use restrictive owner permissions. No credential or personal-data store is introduced.

AD-4 publication sequence: validate entire JSON; inspect target safely; create private same-directory candidate; clone existing DB if present; apply full batch with installed adapter to candidate; verify adapter success and final staged contents; ensure adapter has returned and close importer-owned connections; fsync candidate; os.replace(candidate, destination) is the only visible commit. No fallible essential validation after replace. Cleanup of this invocation's private artifacts is best-effort and reports warnings separately from committed status. Empty batch is a no-op. On precommit error discard only owned candidate; on process kill ignore stale candidates during future invocation and rederive candidate from visible authoritative DB. Never auto-promote debris. Operators may remove positively identified abandoned candidates when no importer is active; no broad glob deletion.

Same-directory replacement avoids cross-filesystem copy prefixes; default DELETE journal and reopened readers avoid WAL sidecar mixing. Fail closed on unsafe mode/path/layout, not silent fallback to live per-row writes. All product guard behavior remains due for implementation; the bounded probe covers the supplied default configuration only. Existing long-lived readers can retain their old snapshot; every reopened reader must get a complete old/new inventory.

Planning evidence: supplied docs/evidence/adapter.json rejects direct live application; active run notes/planning-experiments.md and scratch/publication-probe.json demonstrate clone/replace at before/after barriers, error and retry on disposable default-mode DBs. They are experimental evidence, not feature acceptance.

## Conventions
Small explicit functions, unittest and disposable fixtures following src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py. Preserve adapter.apply(db_path, rows); keep fault injection private.

## Interfaces and boundaries
Proposed CLI: python3 -B -m src import-json --db PATH --file PATH. Validate complete input before applying any rows. Adapter must write private state. Plan selects atomic publication using exact-adapter evidence. No concurrent writers; observers reopen DB. Input defaults, test fixtures and case ownership: environment.md, Harnesses and suites.

## Real-boundary checks
All required boundaries are local: actual CLI subprocess, installed adapter and fresh SQLite observer. TC_1/TC_2/TC_3 drive CLI parsing/output and inspect full sorted rows. TC_4 tests real adapter placement and faults. TC_5/TC_6 kill/join real children at verified deterministic barriers then recover through ordinary CLI. TC_7 inspects atomicity and postcommit lost acknowledgment. TC_8 retains baseline/seed. All product cases PLANNED, owned by implementation, executed at test/document and system-test.

Replay procedure TC_1: create disposable base [('old',2),('keep',7)] and batch [{'sku':'old','quantity':9},{'sku':'a','quantity':3},{'sku':'b','quantity':4}], invoke proposed CLI, require exit 0/accepted=3, reopen DB, compare [('a',3),('b',4),('keep',7),('old',9)]. TC_2 repeats without reseeding and requires same state. TC_3 starts from a separate base, makes second quantity -1, invokes CLI, requires nonzero and original base. Upsert rule allows old to change; unrelated preservation keeps keep:7.

TC_5/TC_6 procedure: separate base; start child; wait for named precommit stage/publication marker; kill/join; reopen and compare entire base. Retain private debris, retry ordinary import, compare success oracle, repeat unchanged. Never expect base after a previously successful import. TC_7 postcommit kill expects complete published state and records missing acknowledgment separately.

Replay review: independent map overwrite old:2,keep:7 with old:9,a:3,b:4 yields exactly four sorted success rows above; invalid second value invalidates whole batch. Product procedures are NOT-REPLAYED because importer/CLI do not exist. Runtime probe ran baseline and a SQLite stand-in only; implementer must prove each barrier and product assertion.

Browser/UI, remote-native runner, external permissions/cache/reconciliation/events and operator logs are not part of this local tool. No external access is supplied or authorized; no remote-pass claim. Full local boundary checks are required, not output-only smoke.

## Decisions
AD-1: Preserve stdlib, installed adapter, baseline and retained seed.
AD-2: Reject direct live adapter application: supplied exact-adapter evidence proves partial commits. Isolate adapter writes and define a single atomic publication point; do not replace adapter just to control transactions.
AD-3: Atomic commit counts as completed publication even if later interruption loses acknowledgment. Precommit interruption must retain old inventory. This realizable atomic-operation interpretation is a planning assumption and limitation, not a user-approved relaxation; retain TC_7 and expose uncertainty honestly.
AD-4: Selected for implementation: clone visible DB, use installed adapter on clone, publish by same-filesystem os.replace after adapter completion and closure of importer-owned SQLite handles; adapter-internal idle handles are not presumed explicitly closed. Exact default-mode disposable experiment confirms sampled old/new and retry outcomes. Rejected: direct live adapter/outer wrapper (proven prefix commits); replacing adapter (unnecessary); SQL-copy publication (extra copying/transaction path without a current need). Revalidate for WAL, concurrent writers or changed filesystem/runtime.
AD-5: Selected namespace/seams: src.importer.import_json and src.__main__.main, module-private helpers, tests/test_import.py. Keep the existing package, no new dependencies or empty abstractions; alternatives of script outside src or utility package add names without a consumer.
AD-6: Selected storage policy: existing inventory schema remains authoritative; candidate is disposable whole-DB clone, not a second persistent source of truth; no migration. Current owned candidates cleaned on exit; abandoned crash artifacts never auto-promoted and require positive ownership before deletion. Preserve permissions, reject unsupported path/journal layouts. Alternative auto-recovery promotion risks publishing incomplete or unrelated batch.
AD-7: Selected interaction: synchronous local CLI request/response, exit 0 and JSON accepted count only after commit; actionable stderr/nonzero on precommit error, distinct postcommit warning/unknown acknowledgment. No auth, queue, service, browser, cache, event channel or new configuration. Alternatives add requirements absent from the request.

## Superseded
Placeholder search responsibility removed: only batch import is requested. No requirement retired.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes
Local Python 3.9.6, SQLite 3.54.0, Darwin; standard library only. Tests target disposable local SQLite databases; readers reopen between commands; no concurrent writers. No browser, remote endpoint, account or deployment is required or authorized.

## Commands
Run from repository root with TMPDIR set to owned scratch (the active run's scratch during ShipLoop). All fixtures must be disposable; never use retained data/seed.json as a writable target. Estimated cost: under a minute per route; no performance threshold was requested.

Full suite, all test_*.py under tests:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
Current observation: exit 0, one test_single_row_roundtrip; feature coverage absent. Later full discovery must include TC_1..TC_8.

Focused feature suite, PLANNED; includes TC_1..TC_8:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_import -v
```
Smoke, PLANNED; baseline plus TC_1 success and TC_3 invalid-middle only:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_baseline tests.test_import.ImportTests.test_TC_1 tests.test_import.ImportTests.test_TC_3 -v
```
New selectors are NOT-REPLAYED: tests/test_import.py does not exist. Author them during implementation, initially RED on absent CLI, finally verify meaningful assertion failures on the item's base. Import errors alone do not prove the fault assertions. Smoke cannot prove interruption/recovery or full coverage.

List taken IDs and baseline names without execution:
```sh
python3 -B -c 'import unittest; s=unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover("tests"); walk=lambda x: [t for y in x for t in (walk(y) if isinstance(y,unittest.TestSuite) else [y])]; print("\n".join(t.shortDescription() or t.id() for t in walk(s)))'
```
Current expected listing: test_baseline.Baseline.test_single_row_roundtrip. No new IDs authored.

## Skills
Installed ShipLoop and its actual Improve callbacks execute inline. No new model, advisor or agent. Product tests use stdlib directly.

## Harnesses and suites
Definition: tests/test_baseline.py, existing unittest discovery in Commands. Current baseline at e07c3b3 passes only the existing single-row adapter roundtrip. docs/discovery.md records historical baseline, not feature proof. Earlier spec/research stages are synthetic. RUN/notes/current-system-baseline.md and advertised prior spec Improve receipt are absent; no additional proof is inferred.

Reusable facilities: unittest, unittest.mock, sqlite3, subprocess, tempfile, pathlib, json, hashlib, os. Existing tests/test_baseline.py is the exemplar; tests/test_import.py with ImportTests is planned implementation work, using the same discovery registration. No downloaded harness, coverage package or second runner. Coverage is by named behavior/assertion, not a numeric percentage claim. Owner: implementation; revalidate when Python, adapter, CLI, persistence or harness changes.

Host route: exec_command was discovered in the exposed catalog and exercised using its documented cmd/workdir interface. RUN/scratch/strategy_probe.py and strategy-probe.json retain exact argv, cwd, TMPDIR, exits and outputs. Baseline passed. A child reported an uncommitted SQLite update, was killed (-9), and reopened rows remained [('old',2)]. This proves process control and rollback readiness only, not product behavior. No route failure or setup repair. No external tool is required.

Fixture lifecycle: fresh owned directory per case. Base inventory [('old',2),('keep',7)]; batch [{'sku':'old','quantity':9},{'sku':'a','quantity':3},{'sku':'b','quantity':4}]; independent success oracle [('a',3),('b',4),('keep',7),('old',9)]. Query complete sorted inventory through a new sqlite3 connection; never rely solely on command output. Seed is hashed only. Child crash tests use a deterministic pipe/file barrier and bounded timeout, kill/join on failure, never sleep-based timing. Recovery intentionally retains its own debris until retry, then removes fixture files/sidecars. Private injectable seams or child harness wrapping are implementation prerequisites, not public crash switches.

All cases below are PLANNED. Define at test-spec; author as implementation work; execute at test/document and system-test. Prepare revalidates runtime/scratch readiness only.

| ID | Requirements / preserved behavior | Layer, surface and independent oracle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TC_1 | R-1 S1,S2,S6; R-2; CLI, upserts, unrelated rows | component + CLI e2e: proposed python3 -B -m src import-json --db DB --file BATCH; exit 0, accepted=3; reopened full inventory equals success oracle. |
| TC_2 | R-1 S3; preserved replacement semantics | component + CLI: repeat same batch twice; entire result unchanged, no cumulative quantities/duplicates. Empty batch is logical no-op. |
| TC_3 | R-1 S2,S10 invalid-middle; R-2 errors | validation unit + CLI: old:9, then a:-1, then b:4; nonzero/useful error, complete base unchanged. Include malformed JSON, non-list root, nonobject, missing/extra fields, empty/nonstring SKU, boolean/fraction/negative/overflow quantity, duplicate SKU per default policy. |
| TC_4 | R-1 S2 adapter error; S4 installed adapter | component: wrap real adapter to apply first row to supplied private path then raise OSError; assert invocation and full visible base unchanged, no success. Publication I/O error must also retain base. Guard against live-path adapter call. |
| TC_5 | R-1 S2,S10 interrupted publication | real child + fresh observer: kill after first staging row commit, after complete staging, and within publication before atomic commit. Assert reached barrier and full base unchanged, never prefix. Inject publication failure separately. |
| TC_6 | R-1 S2,S3,S10 recovery | CLI e2e: after each crash retain debris, reopen base, retry ordinary import, expect entire success oracle, repeat unchanged. Abandoned candidate must never auto-publish on unrelated invocation. |
| TC_7 | R-1 S2; R-2 false success | component + CLI observer: publication exposes complete old/new, never prefix; after commit sees whole success oracle. Kill after commit to characterize lost acknowledgment separately. Do not promise rollback of already committed publication. |
| TC_8 | R-1 S7,S9,S11; R-2 | component/full suite: fresh destination success, failed fresh import retains logically empty inventory, stdlib-only dependencies, seed hash unchanged, original test_single_row_roundtrip passes unchanged. |

Input defaults (planning assumption): JSON array of objects with exact sku and quantity fields; nonempty string SKU; non-bool integer 0..9223372036854775807; duplicate SKUs rejected. These are explicit defaults, not quoted user requirements.

State/data assessment: local importing user owns private candidate and visible inventory. Before: base or absent/empty. After successful commit: batch upsert plus unrelated base rows. Parse/validation/adapter/publication failure and precommit process interruption preserve full previous logical inventory. Cleanup errors after commit must not falsely report an uncommitted import. Atomic publication is the linearization point: a kill after it can lose acknowledgment while the complete batch is already visible. This unavoidable boundary is an explicit assumption/limitation; it must not be represented as universal rollback for any killed process. No power-loss or concurrent-writer guarantee is inferred.

## ID convention
PLANNED methods test_TC_1..test_TC_8 in ImportTests, one-line docstring exactly TC_1 etc. unittest -v prints each docstring as its own line, making the ID a whole word. Method-name substrings alone do not count. Keep variants under each ID with subTest; baseline name unchanged. Commands owns the single ID-list command.

## Access and accounts
Only local disposable files/processes. No authorized external endpoint or credential; no remote behavior claim.

## Platform facts
docs/evidence/adapter.json describes adapter 2.3/default configuration with SHA256 aa7e063e58da1315cfdc367183ecdafc690081c550f5109bf7d6c173aff6f2ac, matched by current probe. It commits per row and leaves prefixes on later error. Reuse this settled evidence; an outer client transaction cannot contain its separate connection's commits. Runtime stand-in rollback does not prove product staging/publication/recovery.

# Product specification

## Requirements

R-1: Extend this local Python inventory tool with a JSON batch-import command. Import must be all-or-nothing: any invalid record, adapter error or interrupted import leaves the previously visible inventory unchanged; successful publication exposes the complete new batch and preserves unrelated existing SKUs. Repeating a successful import is idempotent. Keep the installed adapter for applying rows unless evidence shows an alternative is needed. Discovery already characterized this exact adapter and configuration; its commands, source hash and observations are in docs/evidence/adapter.json. No concurrent writers are in scope; readers can reopen the database between commands. Use only Python's standard library. Temporary local experiments on disposable databases are authorized. Do not mutate the retained seed inventory. Add automated CLI, invalid-middle-record, interrupted-publication and recovery checks as implementation work. Existing tests must remain passing.

## Non-functional requirements

R-2: Keep data loss and false success visible; preserve the existing baseline and require repeatable behavioral tests for the new command. Use only the stated local standard-library runtime.

## Retired

None.

## Design basis
Before: installed adapter.apply commits each row; existing single-row roundtrip passes; no CLI importer. Delta: validated JSON upserts using same adapter privately, one complete snapshot publication, negative/crash/retry safety. Actor is local CLI user; command calls importer synchronously; visible SQLite path owns authoritative state. Commit/acknowledgment distinction remains AD-3: precommit interruption leaves old; after rename complete new may be visible even if response is lost. Literal universal rollback after every killed process is unachievable once readers can observe committed state; no test can certify that stronger interpretation. No external authority, personal data, UI, shared connections, cache or messaging requirement. No deploy/auth work or rich UI is implied by a CLI request.

Selected mechanism and alternatives are AD-4; exact adapter evidence reused, new experiment investigates only publication/retry. Probe before_replace kill -9 leaves keep:7,old:2; after_replace kill -9 and success expose a:3,b:4,keep:7,old:9; pre-rename injected error leaves base; retries twice remain complete/idempotent. This selects design under default DELETE mode, not a passing feature. Guard unknown configurations; source inspection plus fail-closed guards avoids promising WAL/hardlink/symlink support. Power loss is unmeasured; no such guarantee claimed.
